claims.sentence: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 66 Gerrard Street East under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act.
claims.quote: This report recommends that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 66 Gerrard Street East (including entrance addresses at 366, 368, and 370 Church Street and 64 Gerrard Street East) under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act

claims.sentence: This property includes entrance addresses at 366, 368, and 370 Church Street and 64 Gerrard Street East.
claims.quote: the property at 66 Gerrard Street East (including entrance addresses at 366, 368, and 370 Church Street and 64 Gerrard Street East)

claims.sentence: The property is located at the northwest corner of Gerrard Street East and Church Street in the Downtown Yonge East neighbourhood.
claims.quote: The subject property at 66 Gerrard Street East is located on the north side of Gerrard Street East, at the northwest corner of Church Street, within the Downtown Yonge East neighbourhood of downtown Toronto.

claims.sentence: The property is in Ward 13 - Toronto Centre.
If there are no objections to the designation, staff recommend that City Council let the City Solicitor introduce a bill to designate the property.
claims.quote: If there are no objections to the designation, City Council authorize the City Solicitor to introduce the Bill in Council designating the property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act.

claims.sentence: Designation lets City Council review proposed changes or demolitions and enforce heritage maintenance standards.
claims.quote: Designation enables City Council to review proposed alterations or demolitions to the property and enforce heritage property standards and maintenance.

claims.sentence: A property may be designated if it meets two or more of the nine provincial criteria.
claims.quote: A property may be designated under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act, if it meets two or more of the nine criteria.

claims.sentence: Staff and a heritage consultant agree that this property has cultural heritage value and meets five of the nine provincial criteria.
claims.quote: Staff have independently reviewed the research and heritage evaluations prepared by the Consultant and agree with the determination that the property at 66 Gerrard Street East (including entrance addresses at 366, 368, and 370 Church Street and 64 Gerrard Street East) has cultural heritage value and meets five of the nine criteria

claims.sentence: The property has design and physical value as a representative example of a Georgian style rowhouse built around 1855, with a Second Empire style mansard roof added around 1875 and a rear addition built around 1910.
claims.quote: Constructed circa 1855, the property comprises a row of three attached brick house-form buildings, historically known as 62, 64, and 66 Gerrard Street East, designed in the Georgian architectural style and raised to two-and-a-half storeys c. 1875 with a Second Empire mansard roof spanning the three units, together with a c. 1910 rear addition forming a streetwall along Church Street.

claims.sentence: The property has historical value because of its direct links to a person and businesses significant to Toronto's LGBTQ+ community.
claims.quote: The property at 66 Gerrard Street East has historical and associative value due to its direct associations with a person and businesses that are significant to Toronto’s LGBTQ+ community.

claims.sentence: The property also has contextual value because it helps maintain the historic 19th-century streetscape character around the intersection of Church and Gerrard Streets.
claims.quote: The subject property forms part of a collection of mid- to late-19th-century house-form buildings around the intersection of Church and Gerrard Streets that together maintain a fine-grained, pedestrian-scaled, streetscape characteristic of the 19th-century neighbourhood.

claims.sentence: There are no financial impacts to the City from the recommendations in this report.
claims.quote: There are no financial implications resulting from the recommendations included in this report in the current budget year or in future years.
